description: Allows the addition, modification and deletion of auth methods in a Consul cluster using the agent. For more details on using and configuring ACLs, see https://www.consul.io/docs/guides/acl.html.

parameters.name: ca_path
parameters.description: The CA bundle to use for https connections.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The raw configuration to use for the chosen auth method. Contents vary depending upon the type chosen. Required when the auth method is created.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Free form human readable description of the auth method.

parameters.name: display_name
parameters.description: An optional name to use instead of name when displaying information about this auth method.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Host of the Consul agent. Default: "localhost"

parameters.name: max_token_ttl
parameters.description: This specifies the maximum life of any token created by this auth method. Can be specified in the form of 60s or 5m (that is, 60 seconds or 5 minutes, respectively).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Specifies a name for the ACL auth method. The name can contain alphanumeric characters, dashes -, and underscores _.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The port on which the consul agent is running. Default: 8500

parameters.name: scheme
parameters.description: The protocol scheme on which the Consul agent is running. Defaults to http and can be set to https for secure connections. Default: "http"

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Whether the token should be present or absent. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The token to use for authorization.

parameters.name: token_locality
parameters.description: Defines the kind of token that this auth method should produce. Choices: "local" "global"

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type of auth method being configured. This field is immutable. Required when the auth method is created. Choices: "kubernetes" "jwt" "oidc" "aws-iam"

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: Whether to verify the TLS certificate of the Consul agent. Choices: false true ← (default)

examples:
- name: Create an auth method
  community.general.consul_auth_method:
    name: test
    type: jwt
    config:
      jwt_validation_pubkeys:
        - |
          -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
          MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAu1SU1LfVLPHCozMxH2Mo
          4lgOEePzNm0tRgeLezV6ffAt0gunVTLw7onLRnrq0/IzW7yWR7QkrmBL7jTKEn5u
          +qKhbwKfBstIs+bMY2Zkp18gnTxKLxoS2tFczGkPLPgizskuemMghRniWaoLcyeh
          kd3qqGElvW/VDL5AaWTg0nLVkjRo9z+40RQzuVaE8AkAFmxZzow3x+VJYKdjykkJ
          0iT9wCS0DRTXu269V264Vf/3jvredZiKRkgwlL9xNAwxXFg0x/XFw005UWVRIkdg
          cKWTjpBP2dPwVZ4WWC+9aGVd+Gyn1o0CLelf4rEjGoXbAAEgAqeGUxrcIlbjXfbc
          mwIDAQAB
          -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
    token: "{{ consul_management_token }}"

- name: Delete auth method
  community.general.consul_auth_method:
    name: test
    state: absent
    token: "{{ consul_management_token }}"
